title: Subway Vocabulary
summary: Everyday subway words: stand, approach, slow down, get off.
script:
Imagine that you’re going to take the subway, and you're standing at the entrance of a subway station

To stand means to be on your feet, in a vertical position.
You can hear people walking, distant conversations, announcements and trains moving somewhere below you. 
Take a deep breath in and begin walking down the stairs.
Breathe out, and now you are at the platform.
The platform is the area where you stand and wait for the train.
In the distance, you hear the train approaching.


Approaching means coming closer.
The train finally arrives.
The doors open. You hear an announcement telling passengers to board the train.

To board means to get on a train, plane, bus, or other form of transportation.
You step inside and the doors close behind you.
You look above the doors and see a map showing all the stops on your route.
Your stop isn’t the next one. You still have some time, so relax your shoulders.
The train moves through the tunnel.

To move through something means to travel, pass, or progress from one side, stage, or point of something to another.
Listen. You can hear the wheels moving along the tracks while the train begins to slow down.

To slow down means to start moving more slowly.
The doors open. This is your stop. You get off the train and step back onto the platform.
To get off means to leave the train.
Have a good rest of your day.

vocabulary.definition: to be on your feet, in a vertical position
to come closer to someone or something
to leave a train, bus, plane, or other form of transportation

exercises.sentence: You wait on your feet at the platform. You need _____.
